Multiple Imputation by Bayesian PCA

Source: R/mi_pca_imp.R
mipca.Rd

Draw multiple imputations for the missing values of a numeric matrix under a low-rank model using the Audigier, Husson and Josse (BayesMIPCA) data-augmentation sampler.

Usage

mipca(
  obj,
  rank,
  transform,
  subset = NULL,
  keep_state = FALSE,
  prop_diag = 0.5,
  iter_sampling = 100,
  iter_warmup = 100,
  thin = 1,
  nu = Inf,
  chains = 4L,
  refresh = 0L,
  spectra = spectra_opts(),
  init = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  abb = NULL
)

Arguments

obj

A double matrix with samples in rows and features in columns. Row and column names are required and must be unique. NA and NaN values are imputed.

rank

Integer. Number of principal components in the model. Use mipca_tune() to choose the rank on held-out values.

transform

Character or a transform object. The scale the model is fitted on: "identity", "logit_biwhiten", or an object from tf_identity(), tf_sv() or tf_biwhiten(). See Details in mipca().

subset

Optional character or integer vector. The columns whose draws are kept and returned, by name or by number, or NULL for every column. Defaults to NULL.

keep_state

Logical. If TRUE, return a fit that update() can extend at the cost of memory. Defaults to FALSE.

prop_diag

Numeric scalar between 0 and 1. Proportion of each column's missing values on which summary() computes Rhat and ESS. 0 is refused. Defaults to 0.5.

iter_sampling

Integer. Number of draws kept per chain. Defaults to 100.

iter_warmup

Integer. Number of iterations discarded at the start of each chain, 0 or more. Defaults to 100.

thin

Integer. After warmup, each chain keeps one iteration in every thin, so it runs iter_sampling * thin iterations to keep iter_sampling draws. Defaults to 1.

nu

Numeric. Degrees of freedom of the noise drawn for a missing value: Inf for Gaussian noise, or a number above 2 for Student-t noise of the same variance. Defaults to Inf. Can be chosen by mipca_tune().

chains

Integer. Number of independent chains. Defaults to 4.

refresh

Integer. Print a progress line every refresh iterations of each chain, or 0 for none. Defaults to 0.

spectra

A spectra_opts object. Settings for the eigensolver, from spectra_opts().

init

Numeric. How widely each chain's starting values are spread: each missing value starts at a random draw whose standard deviation is init times its column's observed standard deviation. Must be positive. Defaults to 1.

seed

Integer, numeric, or NULL. Seed for the sampler. With NULL, the seed is drawn from R's random number stream. Defaults to NULL.

abb

Optional character or integer vector. Columns to draw by approximate Bayesian bootstrap instead of by the model. abb_cols() proposes them. Defaults to NULL.

Value

With keep_state = FALSE, a finalized fit of class si_mi. It holds chains * iter_sampling draws of every missing value in the selected columns. Use:

  • as.matrix(fit, draw = b) for the completed matrix at draw b.

  • summary() for Rhat and ESS.

  • cbind() to join fits made over different columns.

With keep_state = TRUE, a resumable fit of class si_mi_pca. Extend it with update(), then finish it with mipca_finalize().

Details

The transform. "identity" fits the values as they are. "logit_biwhiten" is for proportions such as DNAm beta values, and every observed value must lie in [0, 1]; see tf_sv() and tf_biwhiten(). Draws are returned on the scale of obj.

Which columns take part. Every column of obj takes part in the model, and every missing value is drawn at every iteration. subset selects only which columns' draws are kept. The result holds the selected columns in the order they have in obj.

Size. The draws hold one number per missing value kept, per chain, per draw. Keep fewer columns with subset, or ask for fewer chains or iter_sampling. If the selected columns have no missing values, the fit is returned without sampling.

Reproducibility. With the same seed, or the same set.seed() before a call with seed = NULL, the draws are the same.

Performance

Linking R to a faster BLAS can make the sampler significantly faster: OpenBLAS on Windows, or Apple's Accelerate on macOS.

References

Audigier V, Husson F, Josse J (2016). Multiple imputation for continuous variables using a Bayesian principal component analysis. Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation, 86(11), 2140-2156. doi:10.1080/00949655.2015.1104683

See also

  • mipca_tune() and mipca_fit() to choose rank and nu on held-out values, then fit.

  • mipca_flank_plan() to fit each target column on a window of its neighbors by location.

  • pca_imp() for a single imputation.

Examples

set.seed(1)
sim <- sim_mat(n = 50, p = 20, beta = TRUE)
fit <- mipca(sim$input, rank = 2, transform = "logit_biwhiten", seed = 1)
fit
#> si_mi fit: 50 x 20, 100 imputed cells, 400 draws
#>   next: as.matrix() with 'draw' for a completed matrix, summary() for Rhat and ESS
completed <- lapply(c(1, 200, 400), function(b) as.matrix(fit, draw = b))
summary(fit)
#> si_mi_summary: Rhat and ESS for 50 cells in 10 columns
#>   prop_diag 0.5, 4 chains x 100 draws
#>           0% 25%    50%    75%   100%
#> rhat   0.996   1   1.01   1.01   1.03
#> ess  153.000 291 330.00 354.00 409.00
#> worst 6 cells by rhat:
#>  chunk col      name row     rhat      ess
#>      1  10 feature10  11 1.029468 230.5473
#>      1   7  feature7   4 1.017100 333.5527
#>      1  14 feature14   2 1.016376 348.8917
#>      1  10 feature10  28 1.016294 219.3950
#>      1  20 feature20   5 1.016222 266.4496
#>      1  15 feature15  35 1.015993 300.7472
